subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This adds a security-sensitive config surface and changes scheduled-run tool-access precedence, which repository policy treats as a maintainer product/security decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as subagent-policy consumers, reducing new schema but coupling scheduled jobs to subagent semantics that are currently distinct.

options.title: Keep current mitigations
options.body: Leave global cron policy out of core and rely on per-job `--tools` plus delivery duplicate suppression, accepting that operators lack a system-wide cron deny knob.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact cron tool-policy gap and current blame points to the relevant config/runtime policy surfaces.
